openwrt_wiki.einleitung: The Extreme Networks WS-AP3935i (internal antennas) and WS-AP3935e (same but with external/detachable antennas) is a dual-band 4x4 MIMO 802.11ac (5GHz) and 802.11b/g/n (2.4GHz) "enterprise grade" access point with two Gigabit Ethernet ports. It can be powered via 802.3af PoE (ETH1, ETH0) or a standard 12V 1.1A power adapter and was produced by Extreme Networks.
openwrt_wiki.oem_watchdog: Redundante Systempartitionen; nach mehreren Neustarts lädt der Watchdog SecImg, das OEM-Image kopiert sich dann über PriImg und zerstört die OpenWrt-Installation; PriImg und SecImg müssen gelöscht werden
openwrt_wiki.installation: RJ45-Konsole (Cisco-kompatibel, 115200 8N1, keine Flusskontrolle), U-Boot unterbrechen, OEM-Partitionen PriImg/SecImg löschen, bootcmd anpassen, initramfs per TFTP laden (tftpboot 0x42000000), bootm, dann squashfs-nand-sysupgrade.bin per LuCI/sysupgrade
openwrt_wiki.anschluss_installation: OpenWrt 24: LAN1; OpenWrt 25: LAN2 (LAN1 ist dort WAN)

netzwerk.eth0: Port LAN1 - OpenWrt 24: none, OpenWrt 25+: WAN
netzwerk.eth1: Port LAN2 - OpenWrt 24: DHCP, OpenWrt 25+: LAN/DHCP

openwrt_wiki.gehaeuse_oeffnen: 4x Torx (T10) screws on back of device and pry case apart. Thermal pads may stick and provide some resistance.
openwrt_wiki.jtag: JTAG surface mount solder pads (Foto ws-ap3935x_board-top-jtag.jpg); requires an SMT header or soldering wires directly to the board
hardware_mods: Adding USB Support: USB header and solder points are present. Data lines for USB 2.0 are accessible on the PCB, but 5 Volt power conditioning components are missing.
Directly powering a 3.3 Volt device with onboard JTAG header and USB data lines (Forum 87234/100)
mPCIe cards are replaceable, allowing modular upgrades to newer WiFi chips and 4G/5G modem support. WiFi 6 5GHz upgrade with AsiaRF AW7915-NP1 (MediaTek MT7975AN) (Forum 87234/101)
